Date: 2027-11-02T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot access paused — procurement routing delay

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from procurement: our PO approval for the pilot is stuck in accounting — expected to clear in 4–6 business days. The team is mid-eval and the environment is used heavily for a demo next Friday. Can Redwood keep the pilot live or issue a brief credit run so our engineers don't lose momentum?

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the PO screenshot. I’m sorry you’re stuck in routing — I know how disruptive that can be. We can absolutely help keep the environment live while the PO clears.

Can you confirm two quick things so I set this up correctly:
- PO number (if any) or internal ticket ID
- Whether the team needs continued write access to the sandbox (yes/no) or read-only will suffice for the next demo

My plan: I’ll loop in Camila for a short run of credits (token-based) to keep things warm. If procurement clears earlier we’ll reconcile usage. Does a 5-day runway sound acceptable to you? We typically issue a one-time temporary credit and document it against the deal.

If that works, I’ll get the approval and share a small credit stub for your records.

Best,

Camila / Dev — forwarding a customer ask. MediQuant (deal DQ-3482) has a PO stuck in accounting and asked for a short runway to finish a demo next Friday. Attached snapshot from procurement.

Customer asks: 4–6 business days until PO clears. Requesting we keep the sandbox live or provide temporary credits. I think a modest, time-boxed credit will preserve momentum. Recommend 5-day runway with a 2,000-token credit (estimated to cover their demo/test load) tied to the deal, to be reconciled when the PO lands.

Questions:

- Dev: any operational caveats if we keep the sandbox fully writable for that window or should we limit to read-only and seed the credit?

Thanks — I can issue the credit once you approve.

— Hannah
